userStories.title: Replace single-column scroll with responsive grid shell
userStories.description: The ProviderSettingsTab root export currently renders `<div className="max-w-2xl space-y-8">` which forces all content into a narrow single column. Replace this with a full-width responsive layout: a sticky horizontal section-tab nav bar at the top, followed by a 12-column CSS grid content area. The tab nav has 6 tabs: 'Execution Engine', 'Model Browser', 'Embeddings', 'Routing', 'Providers', 'Display'. Clicking a tab scrolls the corresponding section into view using smooth scroll + `useRef`. The active tab is highlighted with an accent underline. All 6 section components (ExecutionEngineSection, DisplaySection, SemanticEngineSection, ModelRoutingSection, ProvidersSection, ExaSearchSection) remain, but are now rendered inside the new grid shell.
acceptanceCriteria: ProviderSettingsTab root div uses `w-full` not `max-w-2xl` — full width of the settings panel
A sticky tab nav bar renders at the top with 6 tabs: 'Execution', 'Model Browser', 'Embeddings', 'Routing', 'Providers', 'Display'
Each tab has a corresponding section rendered below with a `ref` attached for scroll targeting
Clicking any tab calls `.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })` on that section's ref
The active tab is tracked via IntersectionObserver — whichever section is most visible sets the active tab
Active tab shows accent-colored bottom border (`border-b-2 border-accent`) and accent text
Inactive tabs show `text-muted hover:text-[var(--text)]` and no border
Tab nav has `position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 10; background: var(--bg)` to stay visible while scrolling
Tab nav renders tab labels in `text-sm font-medium` with `px-4 py-2` padding
All existing section components still render and function — no logic removed, only layout wrapper changed
On screens narrower than 768px, tab nav wraps or scrolls horizontally (overflow-x: auto, no-scrollbar class)
Border separator `border-b border-border` appears below the tab nav

userStories.title: Status bar header with live agent/model/embedding summary
userStories.description: Add a compact full-width status bar that renders ABOVE the tab nav in ProviderSettingsTab. It shows 4 status pills in a flex row: (1) Agent type badge (e.g. 'Claude Max 5x' in green, 'OpenCode' in orange, 'Codex' in blue — pulls from AgentConfig state), (2) Active model name in a pill (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-6'), (3) Embeddings provider pill (e.g. 'OpenRouter · 819 vectors'), (4) API key count (e.g. '3 keys'). Each pill has a colored left dot indicator. On the right side of the status bar, a 'Rebuild Embeddings' ghost button (just an icon + text, no heavy styling). This is purely a display/shortcut component — it reads from the same API data that the sections already fetch, so data is loaded lazily (skeleton state while loading).

userStories.title: SOTA Model Browser — search engine UI with instant filter
userStories.description: The Model Browser (currently the bottom half of DisplaySection) gets a complete UI overhaul into a standalone full-width section. It becomes a 'search engine for models' — inspired by npm search, the GitHub marketplace, and Vercel's model picker. Layout: (1) A large search input at the top (`Search 347 models...` placeholder, magnifying glass icon, keyboard shortcut hint `⌘K`). (2) Below the search: a horizontal provider tab strip (All | Anthropic | OpenRouter | ...) where tabs are bold pills with counts (e.g. 'Anthropic 3'). (3) Below the provider tabs: two rows of filter chips — COST row (All · Free · Low · Medium · High · Premium) and SPEED row (All · Fast · Medium · Slow). (4) Below filters: a result count (`N models` in text-muted) + sort dropdown (Best Match / Cost: Low to High / Cost: High to Low / Context Window / Speed). (5) Main area: CSS grid of ModelCards — 3 columns on lg+, 2 on md, 1 on sm. Each ModelCard is the existing ModelCard component with enhanced styling. All filters are composed — selecting provider + cost + speed + typing all filter simultaneously via useMemo. This replaces the current flat list in DisplaySection.

userStories.title: Display & Theme compact card with inline saves
userStories.description: DisplaySection currently occupies a large portion of the page (theme selector + model browser + workspace model override). After PM-005 extracts the model browser into its own section, DisplaySection is left with only theme + default model + workspace model override — which fits in a compact card. Restructure DisplaySection into a `rounded-xl border border-border bg-panel p-5` card with a horizontal layout: left half = Theme selector (Light/Dark/System as a 3-button segmented control), right half = Default Model selector (the ModelSearchSelect dropdown). Each sub-section has an inline save — changing the theme saves immediately (no button needed, current behavior). The Default Model has a Save button that appears only when the value has changed (dirty state).

userStories.title: Final assembly — section order, spacing, and scroll anchors
userStories.description: Wire together all the redesigned sections into the final ProviderSettingsTab layout. The correct render order top-to-bottom is: (1) StatusBar, (2) SectionTabNav, (3) ExecutionEngine+Embeddings grid (ref: 'execution'), (4) ModelRoutingSection card (ref: 'routing'), (5) ModelBrowser section (ref: 'model-browser'), (6) ProvidersSection+ExaSearch grid (ref: 'providers'), (7) DisplaySection card (ref: 'display'). Tab nav items should map to these refs: 'Execution' → execution, 'Model Browser' → model-browser, 'Embeddings' → execution (same card, scrolls to top of execution card), 'Routing' → routing, 'Providers' → providers, 'Display' → display. The IntersectionObserver uses `threshold: 0.3` to determine the active section. Remove all old `border-t border-border pt-6` section separators — the cards themselves provide visual separation. Add `space-y-4` to the main content area. Verify the full page renders without console errors, all API calls succeed, and all save operations work end-to-end.
